title: The Rhetoric Course
lede: A guided ten-week path through all four rooms of the site. Each week: read two passages closely, pass a quiz on one device family, and run three drills aloud. Progress saves in this browser.

weeks.title: Sentence Control
weeks.focus: Length, diction, and the two great sentence shapes: cumulative and periodic.

read.note: The cumulative sentence at full gallop — clause added to clause without mercy.
The periodic sentence holds everything suspended until the main clause lands.

weeks.title: Repetition Structures
weeks.focus: Anaphora, epistrophe, and their cousins: repetition that builds pressure instead of padding.

read.note: The most famous anaphora in American speech, building until the refrain feels inevitable.
Repetition drained of hope: the same word returning to say nothing changes.

weeks.title: Antithesis and Contrast
weeks.focus: Balanced opposition: making two ideas clarify each other by collision.

read.note: Antithesis stacked clause on clause until the whole age balances.
Balance used for mercy — matched clauses refusing vengeance.

weeks.title: Metaphor and Image
weeks.focus: Saying one thing by another — transfer, embodiment, the image that argues.

read.note: A dock light made to carry a whole national longing.
Image escalating into prophecy: the falcon, the gyre, the rough beast.

weeks.title: Rhythm and Conjunction
weeks.focus: Asyndeton, polysyndeton, and the pulse of prose — what connectives do to time.

read.note: Clipped command melting into meandering ands — both connective strategies in three lines.
The rhythm carries the entire argument — enjambment and omission at maximum compression.

weeks.title: Argument Moves
weeks.focus: The speaker turning to face the audience: questions, appeals, pivots, maxims.

read.note: Argument under pressure — concession, address, and the periodic case for urgency.
Rhetorical questions in parallel: identical structures asserting identical humanity.

weeks.title: Register and Persona
weeks.focus: Irony, understatement, and voice — controlling the distance between what is said and meant.

read.note: Persona built from digression, hedges, and refusals to say the expected thing.
Irony delivered deadpan as universal truth.

weeks.title: Arrangement and Structure
weeks.focus: How telling handles time: where to begin, what to withhold, when to leap.

read.note: Three tenses in one sentence — prolepsis and analepsis fused.
Structure becomes the subject: the story is built like the labyrinth it describes.

weeks.title: Precision and Compression
weeks.focus: Sound, diction, and the discipline of the exact word in the small space.

read.note: A villanelle compressing catastrophe into controlled understatement.
One sentence, one mind, nothing that is not there.

weeks.title: Integration and Mastery
weeks.focus: Everything at once — reading and speaking with the whole toolkit in hand.

read.note: Nearly every family in 272 words: the capstone text for close reading.
The modern answer: every device dissolved into a chorus of voices.
